questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose to study in Germany because i am studying german, so it made the most sense.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it relatively easy. There was an information meeting online beforehand where we could ask questions, which helped a lot.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an intro week, where we were showed the buildings we needed to know. We were also able to ask older students about how things worked.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: There isn't a designated Campus where i am studying, the university is spread out throughout the city. But it wasn't difficult as such to find housing, you just have to be lucky and apply very fast.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I have found it very nice to live in the city center personally, and I would recommend it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very difficult to get any information about when the registration was taking place.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was difficult. It was also a lot later than i expected, a few weeks after i had arrived. I ended up not being able to registrer via the official website because i am an exchange student. This has caused me a lot of trouble, since i now need a document signed from my teachers that i have attended.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: My teachers accepted me into their classes without the official registration, and are now helping me get the classes recognised. This has happened to a lot of other erasmus students.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: not succesful officially as the system didn't accepts exchange students, but there was a workaround, so it worked out in the end. I got all the classes i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have a lot of patience. German universities is weird and difficult, the administrative stuff is almost more complicated than at UCPH.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were more difficult than in denmark, but that could just be because it was a different language. There is definitely more homework though.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was similar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Oberdeutsch: Wie Bayern, Baden-Württemberg und der Süden spricht
Sprachliche Interaktionen
Deutschkurs B2.2
Einführung in die Mediävistik

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would absolutely NOT recommend Einführung in die Mediävistik, it turns out that a third of the german students fail that class. It was very interesting, but would have been impossible to pass, so i had to drop it. The workload was also enormous.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a network for the eramus-students with a lot of social activities and trips to other cities. There were also sport available through the university.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: It is avery good idea to take part in the erasmus activities, as that is where it is easiest to make friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the surrounding cities, go out in nature, look at tourist attractions.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy, as germany and denmark are pretty similar.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: In the beginning it was difficult to remember that the culture of politeness is different in Germany, but i addapted pretty quickly.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness, and willingness to put up with my subpar german.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do not take Einführung in die Mediävistik. 
Go the smaller cities around the big city, they are beautiful.
Climb the mountains, nice view.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared to deal with a lot of complicated administrative stuff. It is all very old-fashioned and impractical. Just breathe and try to relax, it will work out in the end.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making friends from different countries, gaining new perspectives, and getting better at german.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The administrative stuff.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
